input.quote: (ii) Either Party may, without consent of the other Party, assign this Agreement in whole to (i) in the case of RevMed, its successor in interest or assignee or purchaser, as applicable, in the case of a Change of Control or (ii) in the case of Sanofi, its successor in interest or assignee or purchaser, as applicable, in connection with the sale of all or substantially all of its assets to which this Agreement relates, or in connection with a merger, acquisition or similar transaction.
input.rationale: Section 15.2 already gives Sanofi the preferred-level outbound rights (assignment to any Sanofi Affiliate without RevMed consent under 15.2(a)(i), and assignment to a successor in a sale of substantially all related assets, merger or acquisition under 15.2(a)(ii)), and no RevMed termination or re-pricing right is triggered by a Sanofi Change of Control - the only Change-of-Control termination option in Article XII runs in Sanofi's favour on a RevMed Change of Control (12.2(a)(ii)). The clause fails the inbound side of the rule: 15.2(a)(ii) lets RevMed assign the entire Agreement to its acquirer or successor on a RevMed Change of Control without Sanofi's consent, and nothing anywhere prevents RevMed from assigning to a Sanofi competitor (the 15.2 firewall conditions only carve Acquiror IP out of the licence definitions; they do not restrict the assignment itself). Because the Sanofi affiliate carve-out is deliberately retained in our favour, the mutual-successor fallback is not the right target, so we redline to preferred with the shortest edit: RevMed's Change-of-Control assignment becomes subject to Sanofi's consent, not to be unreasonably withheld, and may never be to a Sanofi competitor. We note but do not flag that 15.3(c)(ii)C cuts off post-termination reverse royalties on a Sanofi Change of Control; that is a post-termination payment tail, not a Vendor termination right.

proposal.summary: Condition RevMed's Change-of-Control assignment on Sanofi's consent (not unreasonably withheld) and bar assignment to a Sanofi competitor.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We kept Sanofi's affiliate and successor assignment rights untouched, but RevMed should not be able to hand this collaboration to any acquirer without our consent: we made RevMed's Change-of-Control assignment subject to Sanofi's consent, not to be unreasonably withheld, and barred assignment to a Sanofi competitor.
